# Controller startup error: no permission for sched_setscheduler; should it be run as root?

> **Current answer:** The provided solutions are to enter root, re-source ROS and workspace environment, and restart. This approach grants broader permissions. A more cautious approach is to first confirm real-time scheduling permissions (Real-Time Scheduling Permission), ulimit, user group permissions, and minimal capabilities required for the system, and only authorize components that are necessary. This post cannot be considered a formal solution until official documentation or reproducible experiments are confirmed.

## Safety notes

- Prioritize verifying ulimit, group permissions, and minimal Linux capabilities when dealing with real-time scheduling. Do not consider 'sudo su and run the entire control stack' as a default approach.
- Limit the robot to a lower speed, lower force, and set emergency stop before deployment in simulation and lifting conditions, and record joint and contact logs.
